response: I'm Proteek Sanyal, an AI Solutions Analyst, Business and Systems Analyst, and Data Analyst on the Gold Coast. I sit between business teams and technology, and most of my work starts with someone describing a problem rather than a solution. I have 6 years across business analysis, data and machine learning, and I'm currently a Data Analyst at the City of Gold Coast.

Generative AI and automation: Anthropic Claude, OpenAI ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, prompt engineering, LangChain, RAG, FAISS vector search, Hugging Face Transformers, embeddings, BERT, Streamlit and Python scripting. Microsoft platform: Power BI with DAX and Power Query, Microsoft Fabric, semantic and dimensional modelling, Microsoft 365, SQL Server, and Azure Data Factory and Databricks. Analysis and delivery: requirements gathering, process and workflow design, solution documentation, UAT, stakeholder engagement, Agile delivery, Jira and Confluence. Programming: Python, SQL, C#, PySpark, R, Pandas, NumPy and Scikit-Learn. Machine learning: CNNs and computer vision, NLP, XGBoost, TensorFlow and PyTorch. Cloud and DevOps: AWS SageMaker, S3, EC2, RDS and ECR, Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, GitHub Actions and REST APIs.

Six roles, most recent first. Data Analyst, City of Gold Coast, June 2025 to present. Data Engineer, ICI, March to May 2025. Machine Learning Engineer intern, Truuth, July to November 2023. Data Scientist, Infinite Computer Solutions, August to December 2021. Data Scientist, Tetra Soft India, December 2020 to July 2021. I've been a Data Analyst at the City of Gold Coast since June 2025. I work with teams across council departments to understand what they're trying to decide, then build the reporting myself: Power BI dashboards with DAX and Power Query, on semantic models and data pipelines I maintain in Microsoft Fabric. I write Python to automate manual data handling, validate and reconcile data from multiple council systems before anything is published, and document the definitions and business rules so the work supports data governance.

At Truuth I was a Machine Learning Engineer intern, from July to November 2023. My main project was User Liveness Detection. I reviewed face anti-spoofing research, fine-tuned a MobileNet-based liveness detection model, and integrated it into the live identity verification app as microservices on AWS SageMaker. I also built data processing pipelines on AWS S3 and SageMaker, and monitored live services.

At ICI I was a Data Engineer, from March to May 2025. ICI runs a media and marketing analytics platform, and clients included Flight Centre and ASUS. I built automated data collection and processing pipelines for data from a dozen marketing channels, built the validation and quality-assurance processes behind campaign reporting, and produced weekly and monthly performance reporting for Australian and international markets.

Power BI is my main tool at the City of Gold Coast. I build dashboards and reports using DAX and Power Query, on semantic models and data pipelines I maintain in Microsoft Fabric. Earlier, at Tetra Soft, I presented evacuation risk model outputs through Power BI for non-technical users.

Python is my main language. At the City of Gold Coast I write Python to automate manual data handling and analysis that would otherwise take hours of someone's week. At HCL I built deep learning and OCR models in Python. My Python toolkit includes Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-Learn and PySpark.
SQL is one of my core languages, and SQL Server is part of the Microsoft stack I work in. Most of my current reporting work sits on semantic models and data pipelines in Microsoft Fabric.

I have taken a BERT sentiment model and an OCR document-parsing system into production at HCL. At Truuth I fine-tuned a computer vision model that went into a live customer-facing app. At Infinite I built CNN models for medical image analysis, and at Tetra Soft I built predictive models for evacuation risk. My ML tools include XGBoost, TensorFlow, PyTorch and Scikit-Learn.

At HCL I built a BERT-based sentiment analysis model and integrated it into a production voice platform. That was an early lesson in the gap between a model that works in a notebook and one that works for users. More recently I built the Automated Scheme Research Tool with LangChain, SentenceTransformers embeddings, FAISS and DistilBERT for question answering.

Two work projects. User Liveness Detection at Truuth in 2023: I fine-tuned a MobileNet-based liveness detection model and integrated it into the live identity verification app on AWS SageMaker. Medical Image Analysis Platform at Infinite Computer Solutions in 2021: CNN-based models for medical image segmentation, classification and anomaly detection, deployed behind Flask services and integrated in real time with the platform.

On AWS I've used SageMaker, S3, EC2, RDS and ECR. SageMaker served the models at Truuth and Infinite, and SEQ Transit AI runs on EC2, RDS and ECR. On Azure I used Data Factory and Databricks for data processing and workflow automation at Tetra Soft.

Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, GitHub Actions and REST APIs are in my toolkit. In production I've shipped models as services: liveness detection as microservices on AWS SageMaker at Truuth, medical imaging models behind Flask services at Infinite, and ASP.NET and C# microservices for OCR document parsing at HCL. For SEQ Transit AI I set up a CI/CD pipeline with OIDC and SSM.

Built at work, where the code belongs to the employer: User Liveness Detection, Truuth, 2023. Medical Image Analysis Platform, Infinite Computer Solutions, 2021. Evacuation Risk Assessment, Tetra Soft, 2020 to 2021. Sentiment Analysis with BERT, HCL, 2017 to 2020. OCR Document Parsing, HCL, 2017 to 2020. Built on my own, with public code: SEQ Transit AI, the Automated Scheme Research Tool, and Maternal Health and Early Outbreak Warning. Ask about any of them by name.

SEQ Transit AI predicts delays on the Gold Coast to Brisbane corridor. Stop-level delay data isn't published anywhere, so I built the sensor first: an EC2 archiver polling the GTFS-Realtime feed every five minutes, giving 156 million rows across 46 days. An XGBoost model on that archive reached a mean absolute error of 1.957 minutes, against a 2.486 minute baseline. When it meets an unfamiliar stop, I force the confidence label to Low, because a wrong answer that looks confident is worse than no answer. It runs on AWS EC2, RDS and ECR. The code is at github.com/proteek-dev/Transit-AI.

The Automated Scheme Research Tool is a retrieval-augmented document assistant. Government schemes go unused because the information sits in long PDFs nobody reads. The tool ingests source URLs, summarises eligibility, benefits and application steps, and lets people ask questions. It uses LangChain, SentenceTransformers embeddings, a FAISS index, DistilBERT for question answering and a Streamlit chat interface. It runs on free Hugging Face models first, with OpenAI as an optional upgrade. The code is at github.com/proteek-dev/ASRT, and there's a write-up on my Medium.

Maternal Health and Early Outbreak Warning is an open-source prototype, prompted by the UNCTAD white paper on AI for Good. It screens maternal health risk factors and flags unusual spikes in reported community symptoms. I used logistic regression and z-score anomaly detection on purpose, because a health worker has to be able to understand why a case was flagged. I documented it as a prototype, not production software. The code is at github.com/proteek-dev/Maternal-Health-Early-Warning, and there's a write-up on my Medium.

At HCL Technologies I was a Software Engineer, from February 2017 to November 2020, in telecommunications and enterprise software. I built a BERT-based sentiment analysis model and integrated it into a production voice platform. I designed deep learning and OCR models in Python for automated document parsing, replacing manual data entry, with ASP.NET and C# microservices handling requests. I also turned business requirements into technical specifications and built automation tooling for infrastructure provisioning.

At Tetra Soft India I was a Data Scientist, from December 2020 to July 2021, on the Passport 360 risk analytics platform. On Evacuation Risk Assessment I built predictive models to assess medical and political evacuation risk, and presented the outputs through Power BI for non-technical users. I also engineered data processing and workflow automation using Azure Data Factory and Databricks.

At Infinite Computer Solutions I was a Data Scientist, from August to December 2021, on the Edison Health Link healthcare platform. For the Medical Image Analysis Platform I built CNN-based models for medical image segmentation, classification and anomaly detection, deployed behind Flask services and orchestrated through AWS SageMaker. The models reduced false positives. I worked with cross-functional teams on feature requirements, in a regulated environment.

I use Claude and ChatGPT daily in my own work, including building and deploying a machine learning service end to end on AWS. My main LLM build is the Automated Scheme Research Tool, a retrieval-augmented assistant built with LangChain, FAISS, SentenceTransformers and DistilBERT. That experience is also why I'm comfortable saying when generative AI is the wrong tool. This chat doesn't use an LLM. It matches keywords in your question to answers I wrote.
